errors: No verifiable errors. The fragmentary arithmetic is consistent with central binomial coefficients if '6 5 9' is read as '6 5 4'. The entries in the second row ('65', '7.8/4.4') are too uncertain to check.

results.what: Scratch evaluation of the binomial quotients (2n)(2n-1)…(n+1)/n! for n=1..4, giving 2, 6, 20, 70 (reading uncertain)
Non-mathematical memoranda: Grodno, years 1821-1824, names Daussy and Dawes, postal address and stamps

deep.surprise_reason: The page is the address cover of a letter. It holds only a few routine binomial-coefficient computations and non-mathematical notes. There is no substantive mathematics.

checkable.asserts: possible interpretation of the row 1, 3, 10, … as C(2n-1,n)

transcription_corrections: All notes on the right panel are written upside down relative to the address. In Gauss's orientation the line order is reversed, so '5 9' and the fraction rows come first.
'6 5 9 / 1.2.3' is most plausibly '6 5 4 / 1.2.3' (an inverted or cursive 4), consistent with the sequence 2, 6, 20, 70.
The first fraction transcribed '1/2' may be '2/1' when read in the inverted orientation.
'65' in the row '1 3/1 10/3 65 7.8' is uncertain; it may be '35' or a fraction such as 35/10. The final entry appears as '7.8 / 4.4', with a second line beneath it.
'f Daussy Grand Grand' appears to be a separate line ending with a comma after 'Daussy'. 'Dawes' is struck through on the next line.
